summary: A prepaid monthly VPS plan with a flat price per fixed size; the 1-month term renews at the list price, and a powered-off machine keeps billing.

egress.included: 4 TB on KVM 1, 8 TB on KVM 2, 16 TB on KVM 4, 32 TB on KVM 8, per month
egress.note: There is no per-GiB overage charge. After the monthly allowance, Hostinger throttles the connection to 10 Mbps until the allowance resets on the first of the next month. Not priced by the calculator.

plans.name: Monthly-billed (1-month term)
plans.note: The card uses the 1-month term's renewal price, the ongoing price for a month-to-month buyer. The first month is discounted: KVM 1 $9.99, KVM 2 $13.99, KVM 4 $25.99, KVM 8 $50.99.

notes: Term choice: the card prices the 1-month term at renewal, because it is the only monthly-billed term. The 12-month and 24-month terms are cheaper per month but are paid upfront for the whole term. Their renewal prices per month are: KVM 1 $12.99 / $11.99, KVM 2 $16.99 / $14.99, KVM 4 $30.99 / $28.99, KVM 8 $53.99 / $49.99. The corresponding upfront totals are $155.88 / $287.76, $203.88 / $359.76, $371.88 / $695.76 and $647.88 / $1,199.76.

Prices were read during Hostinger's Black Friday sale on 2026-10-30. The introductory first-period prices may change when the sale ends; the renewal prices are the regular ongoing prices and are the ones the card uses.
The advertised 24-month prices ($6.49, $8.79, $12.99, $25.99) are introductory and apply only when the full 24 months is paid upfront. They are not the ongoing price and are not used in the card.
A powered-off VPS keeps billing. The stop endpoint says: "This is a compute-only power state change and does not affect billing." Workload C therefore pays the full plan price, not 90 hours.

Task-mode calculator presets (code interpreter, browser agent, scheduled scraper) understate Hostinger: the engine bills only the task hours at a pro-rata rate, while Hostinger sells a whole monthly plan. Workload A is hand-worked as one KVM 2 plan, $24.49; the engine prints about $5.59.

CPU is burstable under a credit system, not a permanently dedicated core. The baseline is 60% of allocated CPU; a full balance covers about three hours at 100%; after that the plan is throttled. This does not bind A, B or C, which sit at or below the baseline on average.
One manual snapshot at a time, deleted after 1 day. Weekly backups are free and up to four are retained (two daily, two weekly); daily backups are a paid add-on whose price varies by plan.

The managed AI automation plan runs OpenClaw, Hermes, n8n or Paperclip; it is $4.99/mo on a 24-month term (renewing at $11.99/mo) and $10.99/mo on the 1-month term. It is a separate product, not these VPS plans, and is not priced by this card.
No separate platform fee; the plan price is the whole machine charge. A free domain for one year is included but is not part of the machine price.

Hostinger quotes RAM and disk in GB; the card maps those figures 1:1 to the site's GiB fields. If they are decimal GB, 32 GB is 29.8 GiB and the largest plan is just under the 32 GiB mark. A/B/C asks are smaller and unaffected.
The `hourly` figure on each shape is derived (monthly ÷ 730) only so the shared engine can price partial months. Hostinger does not sell hourly VPS time; the plan is the bill.
